text:
alice-support: FYI ACME (acct: acme-corp) reporting tool/function-call failures since the v10 rollout this morning. ~15% failing, p95 latency +120ms, and unexpected billing spike. Error seen: 422 TOOL_SCHEMA_VALIDATION. Sample request_id: rq_abc123.

deploy-bot: deployment redwood-v10 rolled to 30% canary at 06:12 UTC :rocket:

ben-eng: Ack. Can you paste a minimal failing request + the response snippet and the request_id?

alice-support: Pasting failing payload and response for rq_abc123: 
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-v10",
  "input": "lookup customer",
  "tool_call": {
    "name": "acme_lookup",
    "args": {"user_id": 12345, "include_history": true}
  }
}
```
Response: 422 {\"error\":\"tool_schema_mismatch\", \"details\": \"field 'user_id' expected string got number\"} 

carla-ml: Looks like selector behavior changed in v10 — the model now picks a different tool or returns args typed differently. v9 used to coerce numeric user_id -> string before tool binding; v10 appears stricter. Do we have repro steps?

alice-support: Repro steps I used against prod canary: 
1) curl POST /v1/invoke -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{...payload above...}'
2) observed 422 immediately for ~15% of requests, particularly ones with numeric user_id.

ben-eng: Trying a local repro now comparing v9 vs v10. Early result: v9 request -> tool acme_lookup with user_id: "12345" (string) and succeeds; v10 request -> tool external_lookup or acme_lookup but args keep numeric 12345 and runtime validation fails. Hypothesis: the selector prompt changed and/or model no longer emits coerced types.

eve-sre: Infra traces show a spike in tool-resolution latencies coinciding with the canary window: tool-resolver p95 +80ms and an increased number of fallback attempts to external_lookup in us-west. Might be routing policy interplay.

ben-eng: For immediate mitigation I recommend two actions: 1) pin ACME to redwood-v9 via routing override (safe rollback for customer) and 2) enable a runtime coercion shim that casts numeric args to strings for known fields (hotfix). I'll open a rollback PR now.

dave-customer-success: ACME is pushing for rollback — they're seeing customer-facing errors and rate-limiting users. Ask: ETA for rollback and whether they'll need credit for downtime.

ben-eng: Opened PR #4321 to pin routing for acme-corp -> redwood-v9 and disable v10 for that tenant. Target rollback at 10:30 UTC unless objections. Also adding an alert rule for toolcall error-rate > 5% / p95 latency +50ms.

carla-ml: I can push a prompt/selector patch to make v10 coerce types back to the previous behavior and add unit tests that assert string types for user_id. Prioritizing now.

alice-support: I told ACME we will pin them to v9 and follow up with a patch ETA. They accepted rollback but asked for a postmortem and a timeline for a fix.

dave-customer-success: Noted, I'll assemble impact metrics and SLA credit calc after rollback.

ben-eng: After rollback we should monitor: toolcall error-rate, selector tool distribution (external_lookup vs acme_lookup), and billing anomalies. Suggest retention of full request/response traces for 48h for postmortem.

carla-ml: Confirming – working on a prompt tweak + regression tests. Will update PR with unit test results.

alice-support: Thanks all. I'll update the customer once rollback is complete and we have an ETA for the v10 patch. :thumbsup:

ben-eng: Rolling back canary for affected tenants now and will post status.

deploy-bot: rollback action initiated: canary routing override applied for tenant acme-corp -> redwood-v9 at 10:32 UTC.

alice-support: Customer reported errors dropped to 0.5% after pin. They requested a follow-up postmortem and timeline for a permanent fix.

ben-eng: Leaving this thread open for follow-ups. I'll attach PR/issue links in a follow-up message.

carla-ml: Will post patch branch link once tests pass.

(End of thread)
